versions.content: For each Synchronized Time Base configured • for a Global Time Master • and to be stored non-volatile (i.e., StbMStoreTimebaseNonVolatile == STORAGE ), the StbM shall load the stored backup time from NvM (refer to [SWS_StbM_00172] and [SWS_StbM_00555]). Immediately after loading the stored backup time from NvM , the StbM shall store a new backup time (= loaded (old) backup time + StbMCyclicBackupInterval ) to NvM . In case the restorage is not successful, the Time Base shall start with zero.

For each Synchronized Time Base configured • for a Global Time Master • and to be stored non-volatile (i.e., StbMStoreTimebaseNonVolatile == STORAGE), the StbM shall load the stored backup time from NvM (refer to [SWS_StbM_00172] and [SWS_StbM_00555]). Immediately after loading the stored backup time from NvM, the StbM shall store a new backup time (= loaded (old) backup time + StbMCyclicBackupInterval) to NvM. In case the restorage is not successful, the Time Base shall start with zero.

Loading Backup Time at Startup For each Synchronized Time Base configured as a system-wide Time Master if StbMStoreTimebaseNonVolatile == STORAGE , upon initialization the StbM shall load the latest stored backup time from NvM (refer to [SWS_StbM_00555], [SWS_StbM_00692] or [SWS_StbM_00172], respectively) as the Local Instance of the Global Time , TL, of the Time Base. In case the restoring is not successful the Local Instance of the Global Time shall start at zero.
